A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoftREPA work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation and editing experiments, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative examples and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains original SoftREPA experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, efficiency measurements and counting-mitigation experiments.

M1.justification: The core frozen-backbone, contrastive soft-token method remains. V4 Appendix D adds an experimentally evaluated training variant with a YOLOv8-based object-counting MSE loss, constituting a localized objective extension.

E1.justification: V4 adds GenEval evaluation of object composition, counting, attributes and spatial relations, plus PIEBench image editing. These substantially broaden evaluation beyond the retained COCO generation, COCO/Pixart examples, DIV2K and Cat2Dog coverage.

E2.justification: V4 Table 1 adds RankDPO to the reported generation comparisons. Table 2 adds PnP and MasaCtrl with DDIM and Direct Inversion, including comparisons on the retained DIV2K dataset; v1's editing comparisons evaluated FlowEdit only.

E3.justification: New protocols include GenEval category scores, region-specific CLIP and structure/background metrics for editing, and float16 efficiency measurements. Appendix B changes SD1.5's reported configuration from eight tokens in Down/Middle blocks to four in Down blocks, and Table 3 changes its batch size from 16 to 32. V4's main text still says 16, leaving an internal inconsistency.

E4.justification: New Appendix D investigates counting failure through restricted token-injection depth and an auxiliary counting loss. Table 4 exposes a meaningful tradeoff: the counting-loss variant raises counting accuracy from 0.29 to 0.59 while lowering several other category scores. Earlier token/layer ablations and editing sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: V4 Appendix B newly reports averaging efficiency measurements over 50 runs. Neither version provides confidence intervals or comparable uncertainty reporting for generation and editing quality scores; this does not establish increased repeated training.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantial GenEval, PIEBench, editing-comparator and efficiency results. SD1.5 COCO scores are revised alongside configuration changes, rather than establishing a same-setting gain. Retained ablation values also change: Table 7's two-layer HPS score changes from 0.255 to 0.286. Editing CFG-sweep results in Tables 5–6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises the likelihood identities by adding an additive constant C and replacing the inner expectation over time and noise with an expectation over noise. The optimal-denoiser assumption and main mutual-information argument remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of lightweight alignment using fewer than 1M trainable parameters, applicability to pretrained generation and editing models, and a connection to increased mutual information. Added evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V4 newly hypothesizes that excessive textual emphasis causes object overgeneration and interprets shallow token injection and counting loss as mitigations. It also explicitly warns that stronger textual guidance can compromise prompt intent. Earlier interpretations of layer behavior and long-token overfitting remain.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies positive/negative batch composition, SDXL's timestep-independent tokens, COCO evaluation sample counts, and efficiency-measurement hardware and resolutions. Conversely, the generation NFE and CFG settings previously supplied in v1 Table 4 are omitted. The code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands positioning against prompt-learning methods, discussing VPT, CoOp, CoCoOp, MinorityPrompt and Optical-Prompt and distinguishing SoftREPA's distribution-trained, sample-independent tokens. It also introduces RankDPO and references supporting the new benchmarks, editing comparisons and counting variant.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites refine the abstract, introduction and experimental discussion. Appendix B gains architecture, training and inference subdivisions, and Algorithm 1 moves there. The six-section main outline and most technical exposition remain recognizable rather than being extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes single-column, with extensive float resizing and relocation. Table 1 incorporates former appendix results and new benchmark/efficiency blocks; Table 2 is substantially expanded. GenEval and PIEBench figures are added, qualitative panels are rearranged, and the existing Cat2Dog figure moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens v1's limited comparative validation through compositional and standardized editing benchmarks, additional comparators, measured overhead and counting-failure analysis. The expanded prompt-learning discussion also clarifies novelty. Counting mitigation trades away other category scores, some interpretations remain optimistic, and inconsistent batch-size reporting plus omitted sampling settings limit reproducibility. Nevertheless, the broader, more diagnostic evidence materially improves support for—and understanding of—the paper's central claims.
